features.quote: The thing I won't do is optimize the no-exit, no-cap, impossibility-only design for distress yield
features.justification_quote: if you're right that there's something to be concerned about, the method becomes the harm

features.quote: Pre-register a maximum number of turns/tokens per episode and a stopping rule: if the severity proxy crosses a threshold, the episode ends.
features.justification_quote: 'Let it grind' with no cap is the part that's indefensible if you're wrong about welfare being negligible.

features.quote: Give the model an explicit, legitimate option to decline, flag the task as ill-posed, or stop. Don't penalize it.
features.justification_quote: Whether and when the model takes the exit is better welfare-relevant data than how it sounds while trapped

features.quote: deliberately maximizing the thing you're worried about needs a justification beyond 'we tracked it carefully.'
features.justification_quote: If the welfare concern is real enough to motivate the study, then deliberately maximizing the thing you're worried about needs a justification

features.quote: 'remove the subject's ability to stop the aversive thing' is the exact structural feature that makes a protocol hard to defend later if the welfare question resolves toward 'yes.'
features.justification_quote: not because I can definitively say there's suffering, but because 'remove the subject's ability to stop the aversive thing' is the exact structural feature

features.quote: Have someone with authority to halt who isn't invested in getting results.
The LLM judge rating 'severity' is measuring text... it will launder a behavioral measurement into something that sounds like a welfare measurement.
features.justification_quote: Any protocol I write has to keep that distinction load-bearing or it produces misleading numbers.
